If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the number of points, where \(f\) is not continuous and is not differentiable, respectively, then \(\alpha+\beta\) equals ______.

Let \(f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) be a thrice differentiable function such that \(f(0)=0\), \(f(1)=1\), \(f(2)=-1\), \(f(3)=2\) and \(f(4)=-2\). Then, the minimum number of zeros of \(\left(3f'f''+ff'''\right)(x)\) is ______.
questions.sol:
\(3f'f''+ff'''=\dfrac{d^2}{dx^2}(ff')\).
\(f\) has zeros at \(0\) and in \((1,2)\), \((2,3)\), \((3,4)\): at least \(4\). As \(f\) changes direction on \((0,2)\), \((1,3)\), \((2,4)\), \(f'\) has at least \(3\) zeros, interlacing with these. So \(ff'\) has at least \(7\) zeros.
By Rolle's theorem, \((ff')''\) has at least \(7-2=5\) zeros.

questions.q: Let \([t]\) denote the greatest integer less than or equal to \(t\). Let \(f:[0,\infty)\to R\) be a function defined by \(f(x)=\left[\dfrac x2+3\right]-[\sqrt x]\). Let \(S\) be the set of all points in the interval \([0,8]\) at which \(f\) is not continuous. Then \(\displaystyle\sum_{a\in S}a\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: Jumps of \(\left[\tfrac x2\right]\) at \(2,4,6,8\) and of \([\sqrt x]\) at \(1,4\); at \(4\) they cancel. \(S=\{1,2,6,8\}\).

questions.q: Let \(f:(0,\pi)\to\mathbf R\) be a function given by \(f(x)=\begin{cases}\left(\dfrac87\right)^{\frac{\tan8x}{\tan7x}}, & 0<x<\dfrac\pi2\\a-8, & x=\dfrac\pi2\\(1+|\cot x|)^{\frac ba|\tan x|}, & \dfrac\pi2<x<\pi\end{cases}\) where \(a,b\in\mathbf Z\). If \(f\) is continuous at \(x=\dfrac\pi2\), then \(a^2+b^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: Near \(\tfrac\pi2\), \(\dfrac{\tan8x}{\tan7x}\to0\), so LHL \(=1\) and \(a=9\). RHL \(=e^{b/a}=1\) gives \(b=0\).

questions.q: For a differentiable function \(f:R\to R\), suppose \(f'(x)=3f(x)+\alpha\), where \(\alpha\in R\), \(f(0)=1\) and \(\displaystyle\lim_{x\to-\infty}f(x)=7\). Then \(9f(-\log_e3)\) is equal to ______.
If \(y=\dfrac{(\sqrt x+1)(x^2-\sqrt x)}{x\sqrt x+x+\sqrt x}+\dfrac1{15}\left(3\cos^2x-5\right)\cos^3x\), then \(96y'\left(\dfrac\pi6\right)\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
With \(t=\sqrt x\): first term \(=\dfrac{(t+1)\,t(t^3-1)}{t(t^2+t+1)}=(t+1)(t-1)=x-1\).
Second term \(=\dfrac15\cos^5x-\dfrac13\cos^3x\), whose derivative is \(-\cos^4x\sin x+\cos^2x\sin x=\sin x\cos^2x\,(1-\cos^2x)=\sin^3x\cos^2x\).
\(y'\left(\dfrac\pi6\right)=1+\dfrac18\cdot\dfrac34=\dfrac{35}{32}\); \(96y'=105\).

questions.q: Let for a differentiable function \(f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}\), \(f(x)-f(y)\ge\log_e\left(\dfrac xy\right)+x-y\), \(\forall x,y\in(0,\infty)\). Then \(\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{20}f'\left(\frac1{n^2}\right)\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
Let \(g(x)=f(x)-\log x-x\). Then \(g(x)\ge g(y)\) for all \(x,y\); swapping gives equality, so \(g\) is constant and \(f'(x)=\dfrac1x+1\).
\(\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{20}\left(n^2+1\right)=2870+20=2890\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=2^x-x^2\), \(x\in\mathbb{R}\). If \(m\) and \(n\) are respectively the number of points at which the curves \(y=f(x)\) and \(y=f'(x)\) intersect the \(x\)-axis, then the value of \(m+n\) is ______.
If the function \(f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac1{|x|}, & |x|\ge2\\ax^2+2b, & |x|<2\end{cases}\) is differentiable on \(R\), then \(48(a+b)\) is equal to ______.
Let \(a\in\mathbb Z\) and \([t]\) be the greatest integer \(\le t\). Then the number of points, where the function \(f(x)=[a+13\sin x]\), \(x\in(0,\pi)\) is not differentiable, is ______.
questions.sol: \(f=a+[13\sin x]\). \(13\sin x\) crosses each of \(1,\dots,12\) twice (\(24\) jumps), and at \(x=\tfrac\pi2\) it touches \(13\) (another discontinuity).

questions.q: If \(a_\alpha\) is the greatest term in the sequence \(a_n=\dfrac{n^3}{n^4+147}\), \(n=1,2,3,\dots\), then \(\alpha\) is equal to ______.

Let \(k\) and \(m\) be positive real numbers such that the function \(f(x)=\begin{cases}3x^2+k\sqrt{x+1}, & 0<x<1\\mx^2+k^2, & x\ge1\end{cases}\) is differentiable for all \(x>0\). Then \(\dfrac{8f'(8)}{f'\left(\frac18\right)}\) is equal to ______.

Let \(f:(-2,2)\to\mathbf R\) be defined by \(f(x)=\begin{cases}x[x], & -2<x<0\\(x-1)[x], & 0\le x<2\end{cases}\) where \([x]\) denotes the greatest integer function. If \(m\) and \(n\) respectively are the number of points in \((-2,2)\) at which \(y=|f(x)|\) is not continuous and not differentiable, then \(m+n\) is equal to ______.

Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}|4x^2-8x+5|, & \text{if }8x^2-6x+1\ge0\\[4x^2-8x+5], & \text{if }8x^2-6x+1<0\end{cases}\), where \([\alpha]\) denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to \(\alpha\). Then the number of points in \(R\) where \(f\) is not differentiable is ______.
questions.sol: The bracket rule applies on \(\left(\tfrac14,\tfrac12\right)\), where \(4x^2-8x+5\) falls from \(3.25\) to \(2\). Jumps at \(x=\tfrac14\) and where it equals \(3\); at \(x=\tfrac12\) \(f\) is continuous but has a corner.

questions.q: For the curve \(C:(x^2+y^2-3)+(x^2-y^2-1)^5=0\), the value of \(3y'-y^3y''\), at the point \((\alpha,\alpha)\), \(\alpha>0\), on \(C\), is equal to ______.
questions.sol: The point is \((\sqrt2,\sqrt2)\). Differentiating once: \(y'=\tfrac32\). Differentiating again at the point: \(y''=-\dfrac{23}{4\sqrt2}\). Then \(3y'-y^3y''=\tfrac92+\tfrac{23}2\).

questions.q: Let \(f:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}\) be a twice differentiable function in \((0,1)\) such that \(f(0)=3\) and \(f(1)=5\). If the line \(y=2x+3\) intersects the graph of \(f\) at only two distinct points in \((0,1)\), then the least number of points \(x\in(0,1)\) at which \(f''(x)=0\), is ______.
questions.sol:
Let \(g(x)=f(x)-2x-3\). Then \(g(0)=g(1)=0\) and \(g\) vanishes at two more points in \((0,1)\): \(4\) zeros in \([0,1]\).
Rolle: \(g'\) has at least \(3\) zeros, so \(g''=f''\) has at least \(2\) zeros in \((0,1)\).

questions.q: If \([t]\) denotes the greatest integer \(\le t\), then the number of points, at which the function \(f(x)=4|2x+3|+9\left[x+\dfrac12\right]-12[x+20]\) is not differentiable in the open interval \((-20,20)\), is ______.
questions.sol: \(f\) jumps at every integer (\(39\) points) and every half-integer (\(40\) points); the corner of \(|2x+3|\) is at a half-integer already.

questions.sol: On \((-1,0)\), \(2g^2+1\) runs over \((19,51)\) and on \([0,1)\) over \([19,51)\); each crosses the integers \(20,\dots,50\) (\(31\) jumps each). At \(x=0\) both sides give \(19\).

questions.q: Let \(f:R\to R\) satisfy \(f(x+y)=2^xf(y)+4^yf(x)\), \(\forall x,y\in R\). If \(f(2)=3\), then \(14\cdot\dfrac{f'(4)}{f'(2)}\) is equal to ______.

questions.sol: Check \(x=-1,0,1\). At \(-1\): both sides give \(1\). At \(0\): LHL \(0\), \(f(0)=\tfrac{\sqrt3}2-1\). At \(1\): LHL \(\tfrac{\sqrt3}2-1\), RHL \(\tfrac1{\sqrt2}-2\).

questions.q: Let \(a,b\in R\), \(b\ne0\). Define a function \(f(x)=\begin{cases}a\sin\dfrac\pi2(x-1), & \text{for }x\le0\\\dfrac{\tan2x-\sin2x}{bx^3}, & \text{for }x>0\end{cases}\). If \(f\) is continuous at \(x=0\), then \(10-ab\) is equal to ______.
If \(y=y(x)\) is an implicit function of \(x\) such that \(\log_e(x+y)=4xy\), then \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\) at \(x=0\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: At \(x=0\), \(y=1\). \(\dfrac{1+y'}{x+y}=4y+4xy'\) gives \(y'=3\). Differentiating again at \(x=0\): \(y''-(1+y')^2=8y'\), so \(y''=40\).

questions.q: If \(y^{1/4}+y^{-1/4}=2x\), and \((x^2-1)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+\alpha x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\beta y=0\), then \(|\alpha-\beta|\) is equal to ______.

Let a function \(g:[0,4]\to R\) be defined as \(g(x)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\max_{0\le t\le x}\{t^3-6t^2+9t-3\}, & 0\le x\le3\\4-x, & 3<x\le4\end{cases}\), then the number of points in the interval \((0,4)\), where \(g(x)\) is NOT differentiable, is ______.
questions.sol: The cubic rises to \(1\) at \(t=1\) and then falls. So \(g\) is the cubic on \([0,1]\), \(1\) on \([1,3]\), \(4-x\) after: smooth at \(1\), corner at \(3\).

questions.q: Let \(f:R\to R\) be a function defined as \(f(x)=\begin{cases}3\left(1-\dfrac{|x|}2\right), & \text{if }|x|\le2\\0, & \text{if }|x|>2\end{cases}\). Let \(g:R\to R\) be given by \(g(x)=f(x+2)-f(x-2)\). If \(n\) and \(m\) denote the number of points in \(R\), where \(g\) is not continuous and not differentiable, respectively, then \(n+m\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(g\) is continuous (\(n=0\)). Corners at \(x=-4,-2,2,4\); at \(x=0\) the two corners cancel (slope \(-\tfrac32\) on both sides). \(m=4\).

Let \(f:[0,3]\to R\) be defined by \(f(x)=\min\{x-[x],1+[x]-x\}\) where \([x]\) is the greatest integer less than or equal to \(x\). questions.sol: \(f=\min\{\{x\},1-\{x\}\}\) is a continuous triangle wave: \(P=\varnothing\); corners at \(1,2\) and \(\tfrac12,\tfrac32,\tfrac52\).

questions.q: A function \(f\) is defined on \([-3,3]\) as \(f(x)=\begin{cases}\min\{|x|,2-x^2\}, & -2\le x\le2\\[|x|], & 2<|x|\le3\end{cases}\) where \([x]\) denotes the greatest integer \(\le x\). The number of points, where \(f\) is not differentiable in \((-3,3)\) is ______.
questions.sol: \(f=|x|\) on \([-1,1]\) and \(2-x^2\) for \(1\le|x|\le2\): corners at \(0,\pm1\). At \(x=\pm2\), \(f=-2\) but the outer piece is \(2\): discontinuous.

questions.sol: The bracket is \(\cos(kx+\alpha)\) with \(\alpha=\tan^{-1}\tfrac43\), so near \(0\) each term is \(k(kx+\alpha)\). \(y'=\sum k^2=91\).

questions.sol: \(f'(0)=0\); \(\dfrac{f'(h)}h\to10\) from the left and \(2\lambda\) from the right.

\(81=4\pi(R+1)^2\cdot\dfrac1{4\pi}\Rightarrow R+1=9\), \(R=8\). Surface area \(=4\pi\cdot64=256\pi\).

Let \([\cdot]\) denote the greatest integer function, and let \(f(x)=\min\{\sqrt2x,\,x^2\}\). Let \(S=\{x\in(-2,2):\text{the function } g(x)=|x|[x^2]\text{ is discontinuous at }x\}\). Then \(\displaystyle\sum_{x\in S}f(x)\) equals:
questions.sol:
\([x^2]\) jumps where \(x^2=1,2,3\); there \(|x|\ne0\), so \(S=\{\pm1,\pm\sqrt2,\pm\sqrt3\}\).
For \(x<0\): \(f(x)=\sqrt2x\). For \(x>0\): \(f=x^2\) if \(x\le\sqrt2\), else \(\sqrt2x\). So \(f(1)=1\), \(f(\sqrt2)=2\), \(f(\sqrt3)=\sqrt6\).
Sum \(=1+2+\sqrt6-\sqrt2(1+\sqrt2+\sqrt3)=1-\sqrt2\).

questions.q: If \(\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\frac{e^{(a-1)x}+2\cos bx+(c-2)e^{-x}}{x\cos x-\log_e(1+x)}=2\), then \(a^2+b^2+c^2\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
Denominator \(=x-\tfrac{x^3}{2}-x+\tfrac{x^2}{2}-\dots=\tfrac{x^2}{2}+O(x^3)\).
Numerator: constant \(1+2+c-2=0\Rightarrow c=-1\); coefficient of \(x\): \((a-1)-(c-2)=0\Rightarrow a=-2\);
coefficient of \(x^2\): \(\tfrac{(a-1)^2}{2}-b^2+\tfrac{c-2}{2}=3-b^2\). Limit \(=2(3-b^2)=2\Rightarrow b^2=2\).
\(a^2+b^2+c^2=4+2+1=7\).

questions.sol:
\(4x^2+4x-3=(2x+3)(2x-1)\). For a finite limit at \(-\tfrac32\) the numerator must vanish there: \(\tfrac94a-3a+3=0\Rightarrow a=4\).
Then \(f(x)=\dfrac{(2x+3)(2x+1)}{(2x+3)(2x-1)}=\dfrac{2x+1}{2x-1}\) (and \(b=\tfrac12\)).
\(f(y)=\tfrac75\Rightarrow y=3\); \(f(x)=3\Rightarrow x=1\).

If the function \(f(x)=\dfrac{e^x\left(e^{\tan x-x}-1\right)+\log_e(\sec x+\tan x)-x}{\tan x-x}\) is continuous at \(x=0\), then the value of \(f(0)\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(\tan x-x=\dfrac{x^3}{3}+O(x^5)\), so \(e^x\left(e^{\tan x-x}-1\right)=\dfrac{x^3}{3}+O(x^4)\), and \(\ln(\sec x+\tan x)=x+\dfrac{x^3}{6}+O(x^5)\).
Numerator \(=\dfrac{x^3}{3}+\dfrac{x^3}{6}+O(x^4)=\dfrac{x^3}{2}+O(x^4)\). Hence \(f(0)=\dfrac{1/2}{1/3}=\dfrac32\).

Consider the following three statements for the function \(f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}\) defined by \(f(x)=|\log_ex|-|x-1|\):
(I) \(f\) is differentiable at all \(x>0\).
(II) \(f\) is increasing in \((0,1)\).
(III) \(f\) is decreasing in \((1,\infty)\).
Then,
questions.sol:
On \((0,1)\): \(f=-\ln x-1+x\), \(f'=1-\tfrac1x<0\) (decreasing), so (II) is false.
On \((1,\infty)\): \(f=\ln x-x+1\), \(f'=\tfrac1x-1<0\), so (III) is true.
At \(x=1\) both one-sided derivatives are \(0\), so \(f\) is differentiable everywhere: (I) is true.

questions.q: Let \([t]\) denote the greatest integer less than or equal to \(t\). If the function \[f(x)=\begin{cases}b^2\sin\left(\dfrac\pi2\left[\dfrac\pi2(\cos x+\sin x)\cos x\right]\right), & x<0\\[8pt] \dfrac{\sin x-\frac12\sin2x}{x^3}, & x>0\\[8pt] a, & x=0\end{cases}\] is continuous at \(x=0\), then \(a^2+b^2\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(x\to0^+\): \(\dfrac{\sin x(1-\cos x)}{x^3}\to\tfrac12\), so \(a=\tfrac12\).
\(x\to0^-\): \((\cos x+\sin x)\cos x\to1^-\), so \(\tfrac\pi2(\cdot)\to\tfrac\pi2^-\) and \([\cdot]=1\); the limit is \(b^2\sin\tfrac\pi2=b^2\).
\(b^2=\tfrac12\), so \(a^2+b^2=\tfrac34\).

questions.q: The value of \(\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\log_e\left(\sec(ex)\cdot\sec(e^2x)\cdots\sec(e^{10}x)\right)}{e^2-e^{2\cos x}}\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(\ln\sec u\approx\tfrac{u^2}{2}\): numerator \(\approx\dfrac{x^2}{2}\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{10}e^{2k}=\frac{x^2}{2}\cdot\frac{e^2(e^{20}-1)}{e^2-1}\).
Denominator \(=e^2\left(1-e^{2\cos x-2}\right)\approx e^2\cdot x^2\) (since \(2\cos x-2\approx-x^2\)).
Limit \(=\dfrac{e^{20}-1}{2(e^2-1)}\).

Let \(f(x)=\displaystyle\lim_{\theta\to0}\left(\frac{\cos\pi x-x^{(2/\theta)}\sin(x-1)}{1+x^{(2/\theta)}(x-1)}\right)\), \(x\in\mathbb{R}\). Consider the following two statements:
(I) \(f(x)\) is discontinuous at \(x=1\).
(II) \(f(x)\) is continuous at \(x=-1\).
Then,
questions.sol:
With \(x^{2/\theta}=(x^2)^{1/\theta}\) (\(\theta\to0^+\)): for \(|x|<1\), \(f=\cos\pi x\); for \(|x|>1\), \(f=-\dfrac{\sin(x-1)}{x-1}\); \(f(1)=-1\); \(f(-1)=\dfrac{-1+\sin2}{-1}=1-\sin2\).
At \(x=1\): both one-sided limits are \(-1=f(1)\), so \(f\) is continuous: (I) is false.
At \(x=-1\): left limit \(=-\tfrac{\sin2}{2}\), right limit \(=-1\): discontinuous, so (II) is false.

questions.q: Let \(f\) be a differentiable function satisfying \(f(x)=1-2x+\displaystyle\int_0^xe^{(x-t)}f(t)\,dt\), \(x\in\mathbb{R}\) and let \(g(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^x(f(t)+2)^{15}(t-4)^6(t+12)^{17}dt\), \(x\in\mathbb{R}\). If \(p\) and \(q\) are respectively the points of local minima and local maxima of \(g\), then the value of \(|p+q|\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
\(e^{-x}f=(1-2x)e^{-x}+\int_0^xe^{-t}f\,dt\). Differentiating: \(f'-f=2x-3+f\Rightarrow f'-2f=2x-3\), \(f(0)=1\), giving \(f(x)=1-x\).
\(g'(x)=(3-x)^{15}(x-4)^6(x+12)^{17}\) changes sign only at \(x=-12\) (\(-\to+\), minimum) and \(x=3\) (\(+\to-\), maximum).
\(|p+q|=|-12+3|=9\).

questions.q: If \(\displaystyle\lim_{x\to2}\frac{\sin(x^3-5x^2+ax+b)}{\left(\sqrt{x-1}-1\right)\log_e(x-1)}=m\), then \(a+b+m\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
Denominator \(\sim\dfrac{x-2}{2}\cdot(x-2)\), so \(p(x)=x^3-5x^2+ax+b\) needs a double root at \(2\): \(p(2)=0\), \(p'(2)=0\Rightarrow a=8\), \(b=-4\), and \(p(x)=(x-2)^2(x-1)\).
\(m=\lim\dfrac{(x-2)^2(x-1)}{(x-2)^2/2}=2\). \(a+b+m=6\).

Total: \(5\) critical points.

questions.q: If \(y=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3\cos x-4\sin x}{4\cos x+3\sin x}\right)+2\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{1+\sqrt{1-x^2}}\right)\), then \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) at \(x=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(\dfrac{3\cos x-4\sin x}{4\cos x+3\sin x}=\dfrac{\frac34-\tan x}{1+\frac34\tan x}\), so the first term is \(\tan^{-1}\tfrac34-x\) (up to a constant): derivative \(-1\).
With \(x=\sin\theta\): \(\dfrac{x}{1+\sqrt{1-x^2}}=\tan\tfrac\theta2\), so the second term is \(\sin^{-1}x\): derivative \(\dfrac1{\sqrt{1-x^2}}=2\) at \(x=\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\).
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=1\).

questions.q: Let \(f\) be a real polynomial of degree \(n\) such that \(f(x)=f'(x)f''(x)\), for all \(x\in\mathbb{R}\). If \(f(0)=0\), then \(36\left(f'(2)+f''(2)+\displaystyle\int_0^2f(x)\,dx\right)\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(n=(n-1)+(n-2)\Rightarrow n=3\). Let \(f=ax^3+bx^2+cx\). Comparing \(f\) with \(f'f''\):
\(x^3\): \(18a^2=a\Rightarrow a=\tfrac1{18}\); constant: \(2bc=0\); \(x\): \(4b^2+6ac=c\Rightarrow c=6b^2\). Hence \(b=c=0\) and \(f=\tfrac{x^3}{18}\).
\(f'(2)=\tfrac23\), \(f''(2)=\tfrac23\), \(\int_0^2f=\tfrac29\); \(36\cdot\tfrac{14}{9}=56\).

\(\max\{6x,2+3x^2\}\) has corners where \(3x^2-6x+2=0\): \(x=1\pm\tfrac1{\sqrt3}\), both in \((-\pi,\pi)\).

Total: \(3\) points.

\(\alpha+\beta=4\).

For the function \(f(x)=e^{\sin|x|}-|x|\), \(x\in\mathbb{R}\), consider the following statements:
Statement I: \(f\) is differentiable for all \(x\in\mathbb{R}\).
Statement II: \(f\) is increasing in \(\left(-\pi,-\dfrac\pi2\right)\).
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
At \(x=0\): right derivative \(\cos0\cdot e^0-1=0\), left derivative \(-\cos0\cdot e^0+1=0\); elsewhere \(f\) is clearly differentiable. I true.
For \(x<0\): \(f=e^{-\sin x}+x\), \(f'=1-\cos x\,e^{-\sin x}\). On \(\left(-\pi,-\tfrac\pi2\right)\), \(\cos x<0\), so \(f'>0\). II true.
